$comment: The judgement calls — everything that cannot be extracted from code. Props, tokens, tests and adoption are generated; this file holds what a human decided. Keep it honest: it is what the inventory site and AGENTS.md publish.
summary: Tabular data with sorting, row selection and a sticky header. Renders and announces; never owns the data.
description: Table draws the boundary deliberately: rendering and accessibility live here — semantic table elements, aria-sort, a checkbox selection column, the sticky header — while data logic (sorting, filtering, pagination, fetching) stays in userland. It takes already-sorted rows plus a sort descriptor and echoes header clicks back through onSortChange; TanStack Table or your own useMemo does the sorting. That split is what keeps a design-system table maintainable.
useFor: Rows of records the user scans, sorts and compares: people, invoices, jobs
Bulk actions over a selection (the checkbox column drives a toolbar)
Data whose column headers carry meaning a screen reader should announce per cell
dontUseFor: Layout — that is CSS grid; a layout table announces phantom rows and columns
Key-value pairs — a description list says 'label: value' without a header row
Spreadsheet-style cell editing — that is a role="grid" widget with roving cell focus, a different component with a different keyboard contract
Sorting, filtering or fetching — pass the result in; the table will not do it

keyboard.action: Moves through sort buttons and checkboxes in reading order — the table itself is a document structure, not a widget, so arrow keys stay with the browser and screen reader
On a sort header: toggles ascending/descending via onSortChange
On a row checkbox: toggles selection; on the header checkbox: selects or clears all supplied keys

provides: Native <table>/<thead>/<th scope="col"> semantics — screen-reader table navigation with row and column headers announced as context works only on a real table
aria-sort on the sorted column's th only; the other headers stay silent rather than chorusing 'none'
The sort affordance is a real <button> inside the th, so it is focusable and operable without pointer
Select-all reflects partial selection through the checkbox's indeterminate DOM property
A sticky header that keeps its own opaque background, so pinned column labels stay legible over scrolling rows
consumerMustProvide: An accessible name for the table: aria-label or aria-labelledby on <Table>
Per-row checkbox labels that name the row ('Select Ada Lovelace') — enforced by SelectCell's required aria-label prop
Already-sorted rows: onSortChange means 're-sort and re-render'; the table never reorders the DOM
aria-rowcount and aria-rowindex when rows are virtualized, because the DOM no longer contains the whole table
limitations: Not a grid: no arrow-key cell navigation. role="grid" takes over the arrow keys and demands a complete roving-focus implementation — adopt it only for spreadsheet-like editing, as a separate component
Selection is announced by the checkboxes; aria-selected is defined for grid rows and would be unsupported noise on a plain table
No built-in virtualization — see the do/don't for why that is a feature

doDont.do: Pass sorted rows and the descriptor: sortDescriptor={sort} onSortChange={setSort}
doDont.dont: Expect the table to sort, filter or fetch
doDont.why: Owning sorting means owning per-type comparators, Intl.Collator, null placement and server-side flags — a data library's surface inside a styling component. TanStack Table computes; this table renders.

doDont.dont: Build a div grid with role attributes sprinkled on
doDont.why: Screen-reader table navigation announces the row and column headers for every cell on a real table, for free. A div grid starts from zero, and every missed or misplaced role fails silently.

doDont.do: Render skeleton rows matching the final row geometry while loading
doDont.dont: Swap the whole table for a centered spinner
doDont.why: The table's shape is known, so show the shape: a spinner erases the headers the user was reading, and the swap reflows the page when rows land.

doDont.do: Virtualize in userland past ~200 rows, adding aria-rowcount/aria-rowindex
doDont.dont: Ask the design system to ship a built-in virtualizer
doDont.why: A DS-owned virtualizer couples the system to a scroll library forever and breaks find-in-page and screen-reader row enumeration for every table — including the twenty-row ones that never needed it.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: The compound parts mirror the HTML they render. Name the table — it is what a screen reader lists it as.

examples.title: Sorting (the boundary in action)
examples.description: The consumer sorts; the table reflects. Clicking a header only fires onSortChange — rows move when you re-render them.

examples.title: Row selection
examples.description: SelectAllCell takes the full key list from you — the table never knows the data set, so 'select all' semantics (this page vs the whole result) stay your decision.
